‘No Longer Capturing the Public’s Attention’
In an X post, Venture capitalist
Jason Calacanis
argued that 17 years after its creation, Bitcoin lacks strong utility in transactions or smart contracts and is “no longer capturing the public’s imagination.”
“It’s a boring store of value, trusted as that—which is its biggest value,” he added.
Calacanis posted Bitcoin’s 1-year price chart, showing a 30% decline with a recent rebound, and said, “The dead cat continues to bounce.”
Bitcoin is not a dead cat,
! It has many lives ahead.

focused on the convergence between AI and Bitcoin.
Wood’s Defense
Wood, a long-time Bitcoin advocate, was far from convinced.
“Bitcoin is not a dead cat, Jason! It has many lives ahead,” the veteran investor stated.

Wood also pointed to the latest episode of the Ark Invest-hosted “Bitcoin Brainstorm” podcast, where she discussed the convergence of AI and Bitcoin and noted that advanced AI models can be a double-edged sword for the cryptocurrency.
Wood has previously framed Bitcoin as a "wealth insurance policy" that AI-driven growth investments cannot offer.

children: Saylor, Armstrong Also Push Back
Wood wasn’t the only one opposing Calacanis’ arguments.
Strategy Inc.
(NASDAQ:MSTR) founder
Michael Saylor
emphasized Bitcoin’s evolution since 2011 into an asset with a market capitalization of more than $1.6 trillion.
“Preserving wealth across generations is a bigger ambition than entertaining a dinner party,” Saylor added.

Jason, you’ve watched Bitcoin grow since 2011. It’s now a $1.6 trillion success and the world’s most valuable digital asset. Digital Capital is the killer app. Preserving wealth across generations is a bigger ambition than entertaining a dinner party. The orange tie stays.
Coinbase Global Inc.
(NASDAQ:CEO) CEO
Brian Armstrong
deemed Bitcoin as “Digital Gold,” which is here to stay.
It's digital gold – here to stay, and as important as ever.
